as_told.title: DeLonge emails in the Podesta leak

plain: Hacked emails from 2015 and 2016 are said to show a rock musician, Tom DeLonge, working with a senior political adviser, John Podesta, on a UFO project with top defence figures. The researcher Jason Simosa says the emails, leaked after Podesta's account was hacked, held about 35 messages between DeLonge and Podesta's team. He says they show a meeting with Podesta, DeLonge, a retired Air Force general named Neil McCasland, someone named Michael Carey, and Robert Weiss, president of Skunk Works, a secret aircraft design unit. The researcher Grant Cameron calls Podesta, McCasland and Weiss "the three kings" whom the leak exposed. Jay Anderson, released through WikiLeaks, says DeLonge wrote that he wanted young people to be "more pro-military, more pro-government", tying it to DeLonge's book series Sekret Machines. The researcher RedPandaKoala quotes DeLonge as wanting "the government to come off as cool". To these tellers the emails suggest powerful people were behind efforts to shape what the public hears about UFOs.
